newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries well-bid as shorts cover in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries well-bid as shorts cover in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were well-bid by the Tokyo midday on Tuesday, due to short covering ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting today, traders said.
Operators concentrated on position adjustments before the FOMC, but active follow-through buying was limited as many investors held to the sidelines, they said.

"The market has been factoring in a 25 basis-point hike in the Fed funds rate at the meeting," a trader at a major Japanese brokerage said. "Operators could unwind some short positions if the Fed actually tightens. But we have to see the content of the Fed's statement after the possible hike."
"There is a possiblity that the current credit-tightening fears could remain and dampen prices even if the Fed keeps its credit policy unchanged today," the trader said.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 96-11/32, yielding 6.92 percent, compared with 96-8/32 in New York on Monday.

The overnight uptrend continued into Tokyo trading hours, although Japanese investors were largely taking a wait-and-see stance. Traders were also looking towards the outcome of a series of Treasury note auctions scheduled later this week.
The June T-bond futures contract was at 109-9/32, up 10/32 from the previous close.
